dialogues.title: Weekend plans
dialogues.focus: going to → gonna · want to → wanna

lines.text: What are you going to do this weekend?
lines.zh: 你这个周末打算做什么？

lines.text: I'm going to meet a friend for coffee.
Do you want to come with us?
I'd love to. What time are you meeting?
lines.zh: 我很乐意。你们几点见面？

lines.text: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?
Of course. Would you like any milk?
Just a little, thank you.
Here you are. Have a nice day!
Can you pick it up for me?
Sure. Where should I put it?
Put it on the table, please.
No problem. I'll do it now.
Can you tell me how to get to the station?
lines.zh: 你能告诉我去车站怎么走吗？

lines.text: Go straight, then turn left at the end of the street.
lines.zh: 直走，然后在街道尽头左转。

lines.text: Is it far from here?
Not at all. It's about five minutes away.
lines.zh: 一点也不远。大约五分钟。

lines.text: What are you doing after work?
When I finish work, I'm going to meet a friend for dinner.
lines.zh: 下班后，我准备和朋友吃晚饭。

lines.text: That sounds nice. Where are you going?
lines.zh: 听起来不错。你们去哪里？

lines.text: There's a new place near the station. Do you want to join us?
lines.zh: 车站附近有家新店。你想一起吗？

dialogues.title: Catching up
dialogues.focus: did you → didja · las(t) night · tell (h)im

lines.text: Did you get a chance to talk to him last night?
lines.zh: 你昨晚有机会和他聊聊吗？

lines.text: Yes, we talked about next week.
Could you tell him I might be late?
lines.zh: 你能告诉他我可能会迟到吗？

lines.text: Of course. I'll send him a message.
Would you like to go out for dinner?
That sounds great, but I've got to finish my work first.
lines.zh: 听起来不错，不过我得先完成工作。

lines.text: We can meet at eight, if that works for you.
lines.zh: 如果你方便，我们可以八点见。

lines.text: Perfect. I'll book a table.
I would have sent it earlier, but my connection dropped.
lines.zh: 我本来会早点发，但刚才断网了。

lines.text: That's all right. Could you go over the main points?
lines.zh: 没关系。你能把要点再讲一下吗？

lines.text: First, we need to agree on the budget, then set a date.
lines.zh: 首先我们需要商定预算，然后定日期。

lines.text: Let's talk about it after the meeting.

lessons.title: Join the edges
lessons.zh: 辅音 + 元音：把词连起来
lessons.notice: 末尾的辅音直接滑向下一个元音，中间不重新起声。听起来连在一起，单词并没有消失。
steps: 先说 it‿up，让 /t/ 直接连向 up 的 /ʌ/。
再加 pick，让 /k/ 接到 it 的 /ɪ/：pick‿it‿up。
保持一口气说完；不要在 pick 后面额外加一个“呃”。
lessons.practice: Can you pick it up for me?
transfer: Put it on the table, please.
Could I have a cup of coffee, please?
lessons.question: pick it up 中，哪里可以连接？
lessons.why: pick 的 /k/ 后面是 it 的元音；it 的 /t/ 后面又是 up 的元音。两处都可以自然连接。

lessons.title: Let little words shrink
lessons.notice: cup 和 coffee 承载主要意思。a 和 of 通常短而轻，不需要与它们一样响亮。
steps: 先把 cup 和 coffee 说清楚，找到两个信息重心。
在 cup 前轻轻放入 a /ə/，不要刻意读成字母 A。
把 of /əv/ 轻轻带过，连成 a cup‿of coffee。
lessons.practice: Could I have a cup of coffee, please?
transfer: I'm going to meet a friend for coffee.
We can meet at eight, if that works for you.
lessons.question: 没有特别强调时，哪个词应更短、更轻？
lessons.why: of 是连接关系的小词，常弱读为 /əv/。不是把它完全删掉，而是给它更少时间。

lessons.title: Catch the shortcut
lessons.zh: 缩读：听懂 going to → gonna
lessons.notice: 表达打算、后面跟动词时，going to 在随意口语中可能缩成 gonna。标准书写仍使用 going to。
steps: 先确定结构：going to meet，to 后面是动作 meet。
把 going to 当成一个轻快的声音块，不要在中间停顿。
把注意力放回 meet 和 friend；缩读不是全句都加速。
lessons.apart: I'm going to meet a friend.
lessons.practice: I'm going to meet a friend for coffee.
transfer: What are you going to do this weekend?
Do you want to come with us?
lessons.question: 哪一句适合用 gonna 来理解口语发音？
options: I'm going to meet a friend.
lessons.why: meet 是动词，表示打算见朋友。school 和 the station 是目的地，不能直接替换成 gonna。

lessons.title: Two sounds, one move
lessons.zh: 同化：did you 如何靠拢
lessons.notice: did 末尾的 /d/ 和 you 开头的 /j/ 在快一些的连贯语流里可能合成 /dʒ/，接近 jam 的起始音。
steps: 先分别找到 did 的尾音 /d/ 和 you 的起始音 /j/。
缩小两词之间的间隔，让舌头只做一次连续动作。
再放回问题：Did you get a chance? 重点仍落在内容词。
lessons.practice: Did you get a chance to talk to him last night?
transfer: Could you tell him I might be late?
Would you like to go out for dinner?
lessons.question: 这里合在一起的是哪两个音？
lessons.why: 这是相邻辅音的变化。didja 只能当近似发音提示，不要把它写进正式句子。

lessons.title: Notice the missing sound
lessons.zh: 省音：有些 /t/ 会变得听不见
lessons.notice: last night 中，/t/ 夹在 /s/ 和 /n/ 之间，有时会被省略。不是所有说话者都会省，也不是每个 t 都能省。
steps: 先清楚地说 last night，注意 /s/、/t/、/n/ 连续出现。
再尝试从 /s/ 平滑接向 /n/，不刻意爆破 /t/。
听懂这个变化即可；自己清楚地保留 /t/ 也完全可以。
lessons.practice: Did you get a chance to talk to him last night?
transfer: Yes, we talked about next week.
It must be a good idea.
lessons.question: last night 中听不清 /t/，可能说明什么？
options: last 这个词被整个删除了
lessons.why: 减少的是一个音，不是整个单词。音频示范可能保留 /t/；识别不同说法比强行省音更重要。

lessons.title: Hear the hidden pronoun
lessons.zh: 弱读代词：tell him 中的 h
lessons.notice: 在句子中、不强调 him 时，开头的 /h/ 有时不发，tell 的 /l/ 就能直接连接后面的元音。
steps: 先说完整的 tell him，知道两个词分别是什么。
在不强调 him 时，试着把 /l/ 直接接到 /ɪ/。
如果想强调“是他”，保留 him 的完整读音并给它重音。
lessons.practice: Could you tell him I might be late?
transfer: Did you get a chance to talk to him last night?
Of course. I'll send him a message.
lessons.question: 什么时候更适合保留并强调 him？
lessons.why: 语流变化取决于意思。要突出代词时，使用完整读音会更清楚。
